content.text: By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
Describe the structures of diamond, graphite, and silicon dioxide
Explain the properties of giant covalent substances
Compare the structures and properties of diamond and graphite
Explain why graphite conducts electricity but diamond does not

(also called macromolecular structures) are very different from simple covalent molecules. Instead of small molecules, they consist of billions of atoms all connected by covalent bonds in a continuous network.
Many atoms bonded together by covalent bonds
No separate molecules - just one giant structure
Very high melting and boiling points
Each carbon atom is bonded to 4 other carbon atoms
Strong covalent bonds in all directions
[DIAGRAM: Diamond structure showing tetrahedral bonding of carbon atoms]
Many strong covalent bonds to break
Each carbon atom is bonded to 3 other carbon atoms
One electron from each carbon is delocalised
[DIAGRAM: Graphite structure showing layers of hexagonal carbon rings]
Many strong covalent bonds within layers
Weak forces between layers allow sliding
Both are made entirely of carbon, but have very different properties!
Why Graphite Conducts But Diamond Doesn't
Each carbon uses all 4 outer electrons for bonding
No free electrons to carry charge
Each carbon uses only 3 outer electrons for bonding
The 4th electron is delocalised (free to move)
These delocalised electrons can carry charge
Each silicon atom is bonded to 4 oxygen atoms
Each oxygen is bonded to 2 silicon atoms
SiO₂ represents the ratio of atoms, not a molecule
General Properties of Giant Covalent Structures
All giant covalent structures share these properties:
Many strong covalent bonds must be broken
Too many bonds to break for dissolving
Thinking graphite is soft because it has weak covalent bonds
The covalent bonds are strong; it's the weak forces BETWEEN layers that make it soft
Diamond has no free electrons and does not conduct
Thinking SiO₂ means molecules of 1 silicon and 2 oxygen atoms
SiO₂ is a giant structure; the formula represents the ratio
Giant covalent structures have many atoms bonded by strong covalent bonds
4 bonds per carbon, very hard, does not conduct, used for cutting
3 bonds per carbon in layers, soft, conducts (delocalised electrons), used as lubricant and electrode
Similar to diamond, very hard, high melting point
All have very high melting points due to many strong covalent bonds
Only graphite conducts electricity (due to delocalised electrons)
